claims.text: What the strip looks like A fixed PR interval with an intermittent dropped QRS.
claims.quote: Fixed PR interval with intermittent dropped QRS

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Rate: bradycardia may or may not be present
claims.quote: Bradycardia may or may not be present.

claims.text: Rhythm: irregular at each dropped beat — the R-R around it is an exact multiple of the preceding R-R
claims.quote: The RR interval surrounding the dropped beat(s) is an exact multiple of the preceding RR interval

claims.text: Conduction ratio: may have no pattern or a fixed ratio such as 2:1 or 3:1
claims.quote: There may be no pattern to the conduction blockade, or alternatively there may be a fixed relationship between the P waves and QRS complexes, e.g. 2:1 block, 3:1 block.

claims.text: P waves: march through at a constant rate
claims.quote: The P waves ‘march through’ at a constant rate

claims.text: Dropped beats: intermittent non-conducted P waves, without progressive PR lengthening
claims.quote: A form of 2nd degree AV block in which there is intermittent non-conducted P waves without progressive prolongation of the PR interval

claims.text: PR interval: constant in the conducted beats — no progressive lengthening
claims.quote: The PR interval in the conducted beats remains constant

claims.text: QRS: usually broad (block below the His bundle in about 75%); narrow when the block is within the His bundle (about 25%)
claims.quote: In around 75% of cases, the conduction block is located distal to the Bundle of His, producing broad QRS complexes. In the remaining 25% of cases, the conduction block is located within the His Bundle itself, producing narrow QRS complexes.

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Mechanism: failure of conduction in the His-Purkinje system (below the AV node)
claims.quote: Mobitz II is usually due to failure of conduction at the level of the His-Purkinje system (i.e. below the AV node)

claims.text: Usually structural damage to the conducting system (e.g., infarction, fibrosis, necrosis)
claims.quote: Mobitz II is more likely to be due to structural damage to the conducting system (e.g. infarction, fibrosis, necrosis)

claims.text: Anterior MI (septal necrosis of the bundle branches), idiopathic fibrosis (Lenègre-Lev disease), cardiac surgery near the septum (e.g., mitral valve repair), inflammatory disease (rheumatic fever, myocarditis, Lyme disease), autoimmune disease (SLE, systemic sclerosis), infiltrative disease (amyloidosis, hemochromatosis, sarcoidosis), hyperkalemia, drugs (beta blockers, calcium channel blockers, digoxin, amiodarone)
claims.quote: Anterior MI (due to septal infarction with necrosis of the bundle branches) Idiopathic fibrosis of the conducting system (Lenègre-Lev disease) Cardiac surgery, especially surgery occurring close to the septum e.g. mitral valve repair Inflammatory conditions (rheumatic fever, myocarditis, Lyme disease) Autoimmune (SLE, systemic sclerosis) Infiltrative myocardial disease (amyloidosis, haemochromatosis, sarcoidosis) Hyperkalaemia Drugs: beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers, digoxin, amiodarone
Mobitz type II second-degree AV block is always pathologic

claims.text: Symptoms Asymptomatic, or light-headedness, presyncope and syncope depending on how many beats are blocked
claims.quote: Patients may be asymptomatic or experience light-headedness, presyncope, and syncope, depending on the ratio of conducted to blocked beats.

claims.text: Sudden instability: syncope (Stokes-Adams attacks) or sudden cardiac death
claims.quote: Onset of haemodynamic instability may be sudden and unexpected, causing syncope (Stokes-Adams attacks) or sudden cardiac death

claims.text: Risk of asystole is about 35% per year
claims.quote: The risk of asystole is around 35% per year

claims.text: Treatment Immediate admission for cardiac monitoring, backup temporary pacing, then a permanent pacemaker
claims.quote: Mobitz II mandates immediate admission for cardiac monitoring, backup temporary pacing and ultimately insertion of a permanent pacemaker
